definition: Rectified Linear Unit, an activation function that outputs the input directly if positive and zero otherwise.
details: ReLU became the default activation for deep networks because it mitigates the vanishing-gradient problem and is computationally cheap, though it can suffer from 'dying ReLU' units that stop updating.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Think of it this way: Rectified Linear Unit, an activation function that outputs the input directly if positive and zero otherwise. And here is the clever part: ReLU became the default activation for deep networks because it mitigates the vanishing-gradient problem and is computationally cheap, though it can suffer from 'dying ReLU' units that stop updating. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — ReLU — is what makes everything else possible.
